source_text: . Haec unanimitas sub apostolis olim fuit: sic nouus credentium populus Domini mandata custodiens caritatem suam tenuit. probat scriptura quae dicit: turba autem eorum qui crediderant anima ac mente una agebant. et iterum: et erant perseuerantes omnes unanimes in oratione cum mulieribus et Maria quae fuerat mater Iesu et fratribus eius. et ideo efficacibus precibus orabant, ideo impetrare cum fiducia poterant quodcumque de Dei misericordia postulabant.
thought_title: The early Church's unanimity in prayer
orientation: Cyprian is describing the unity of the early believers under the apostles, before he contrasts it with the decline of his own time.
pass_a_gloss: This unanimity existed long ago under the apostles: thus the new people of believers, keeping the commands of the Lord, held fast to its love. Scripture proves it, which says: 'But the crowd of those who had believed acted with one soul and mind.' And again: 'And they were all persevering, unanimous in prayer, with the women and Mary, who had been the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.' And therefore they prayed with effective prayers; therefore they were able to obtain with confidence whatever they asked from the mercy of God.

lemmas.gloss: to obtain, to gain by asking

choices.why: The source term is the abstract noun for oneness of mind; 'unanimity' preserves the Latin root and the theme of unity.
The verb tenuit implies holding firmly; 'held fast to' captures the force of maintaining love as a possession.

choices.english: acted with one soul and mind
choices.why: The phrase uses two nouns for the inner person; 'soul and mind' preserves the distinction and the unity of both.
rejected: were of one heart and soul

choices.why: The adjective efficax means producing an effect; 'effective prayers' keeps the causal link to the next clause about obtaining.

choices.english: were able to obtain with confidence
choices.why: Impetrare means to gain by asking; 'obtain' preserves the sense of successful petition, and 'with confidence' renders fiducia.

et erant perseuerantes omnes unanimes in oratione cum mulieribus et Maria quae fuerat mater Iesu et fratribus eius

pass_b_english: This unanimity once existed under the apostles. So the new people of believers, keeping the Lord's commands, held fast to its love. Scripture proves this when it says: "The crowd of those who had believed acted with one soul and mind" (Acts 4:32). And again: "They were all persevering with one mind in prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus and his brothers" (Acts 1:14). That is why they prayed with effective prayers; that is why they were able to obtain with confidence whatever they asked from God's mercy.
